value.text: It may not be in your best interest to replace existing life insurance policies or annuity contracts in connection with the purchase of a new life insurance policy, whether issued by the same or different insurance company. A replacement will occur if, as part of your purchase of a new life insurance policy, existing coverage has been, or is likely to be, lapsed, surrendered, forfeited, assigned, terminated, changed or modified into paid-up insurance or other forms of benefits, loaned against or withdrawn from, reduced in value, by use of cash values or other policy values, changed in the length of time or in the amount of insurance that would continue or continued with a stoppage or reduction in the amount of premium paid. Prior to completing a replacement transaction, you may want to contact the insurance company or agent who sold you the life insurance or annuity contract that will be replaced to help you decide whether the replacement is in your best interest.

definition.behavior: Next and Back use the form-flow resolver and skip pages whose display conditions evaluate to false.

Pages can register an onBeforeNext hook that pauses forward navigation, shows an intermediate step (e.g. a confirmation dialog or send dialog), and resumes navigation only when the page calls the provided continueNavigation callback. Used by Coverage (dependent-only confirmation) and Profile (advisor send dialog).
If Beneficiary or Payment is configured as none, the page is skipped from the active form flow.

Beneficiary requires a requested amount and an applicant/product allowed by the captured beneficiary participation policy, unless the page is configured as none. The shared fallback gate selects Life (LI) or Accidental Death (AD); explicit Site, Association and applicant exceptions remain authoritative.

Shown for an active applicant whose resolved health page is health-si, falling back to the captured SI gate when no health-page override exists. Assigned source questionnaires may supersede this page.
Shown when a Whole Life product with SI and UW flow is selected. (Page not yet implemented in prototype.)

health-li and health-di use each active applicant's resolved health-page outcome. Without a health-page override, their captured gates require LI + TELE and DI + TELE respectively; assigned source questionnaires can supersede health-di.
Shown when a Critical Illness product is selected. (Page not yet implemented in prototype.)
definition.ref: src/content/docs/siteRules.ts (documented future rule; page not implemented)

definition.behavior: Shown when the captured CIR rider gate matches an enabled rider selection and the page participates in the Site flow. WAEPA's dedicated CIR questionnaire retains its separately approved provisional deferral.

Shown for an active applicant whose resolved health page is health-qd, falling back to the captured QD gate when no health-page override exists. Assigned source questionnaires may supersede this page; the external GMA-JI-L questionnaire shows only the approved prototype loading state.
Shown when LI (QD) is selected with a CIR rider. (Page not yet implemented in prototype.)
Shown when LI (QD) and DI (UW) are both selected. (Page not yet implemented in prototype.)
Multiple routed health pages are presented within the consolidated application-review/progress experience rather than as separate major progress stages.
If every page in a progress stage is skipped, the stage is removed from the active progress steps.
After Review is submitted, Back navigation is disabled on pages after Review.

definition.rule: Back button hidden with no previous page
definition.behavior: The PageHeader/PageTitle back arrow is rendered only when getPreviousFormPageId resolves a previous page for the current values and the page is not after a submitted review; otherwise the back control is hidden, including on post-review pages after submission.

definition.rule: Single template embeds the application in landing-page sections
definition.behavior: template=single embeds SinglePageApplication below the landing content. SinglePageSections renders the active applicant page within a vertical progress layout; completing a page advances to the next applicable section, and permitted edits reopen earlier sections. Shared page participation, validation and routing rules still apply. The theme also forces narrow-screen layout for md/lg/xl responsive styles.

definition.rule: sm breakpoint stays real so sm-level padding isn't lost
definition.behavior: forceMobileLayout only overrides md/lg/xl — sm (600px) is left at its default. Components that only bump padding/spacing at sm (e.g. FormRoutePage's FormShell, which uses px: { xs: 2, sm: "48px" }) still receive that breathing room once the real browser viewport is 600px or wider, instead of staying pinned to their tightest xs padding on an actual desktop screen.

definition.rule: Single template places the application below the landing content
definition.behavior: In single template, Home renders the configured landing content followed by SinglePageApplication. The application reuses the existing applicant page components within one vertical section layout. Artwork follows the configured single-page artwork setting; a fixed hero/form width is not an independent business rule.
Field validation failure blocks advancement, shows an error and scrolls toward the first invalid field. Page-level validation failure blocks advancement, shows its message and scrolls to the top.
Current page values are written to shared application state on submit, Back, and unmount when the page was not explicitly saved.

After forward navigation, the destination page displays a Progress Saved snackbar (AppSnackbar, severity=success). The snackbar appears at top-center on large screens and bottom-center on small screens.
Submitting Membership triggers the current prototype autosave mock-email behavior.

definition.rule: Member section title hidden for member-only flow
definition.behavior: The Member/Self applicant section label is hidden when no spouse/child is actually selected for any product. It is shown when another applicant is applying.

definition.rule: Dependent section shown only when applying
definition.behavior: Spouse/child applicant labels and post-Coverage applicant sections are shown only when that applicant is actually selected for an applicable product.

definition.rule: Eligibility selection alone is not enough after Coverage
definition.behavior: A spouse/child selected on Eligibility does not count as applying if that dependent is not selected for any product on Coverage.
When no dependents are selected, the member is treated as the applicant by default.

When Child is selected and applicantExperience.childEligibility.mode is details (the default), DynamicList collects children[].firstName, lastName, birthDate and gender using the effective field definitions. The full-time-student question is added when applicable product eligibility rules require it. Records support Add, Edit and Remove; at least one child is required to continue. Client or Site configuration can choose notice-only instead, showing the configured note without collecting or requiring records. CSEA uses notice-only.
If Spouse is selected, spouse name details must be provided before continuing.
When the Child dependent section is visible, an info alert under the section header states that only unmarried children are eligible for coverage.

When a recognizable ZIP/postal code is entered, the state/province field is automatically derived when a matching configured option exists. The user may manually override the derived state at any time; a subsequent ZIP change will re-derive state from the new ZIP.

Dependent options on Eligibility can be suppressed based on membership attestation. When a membership type implies a specific relationship (e.g. the member is a spouse/dependent of the primary member), the corresponding dependent option is removed to prevent duplicate applicant entry. Section visibility, labels, and suppression rules are client-configurable.

definition.rule: Category selection and two-step product reveal
definition.behavior: The user first selects one or more coverage categories via a multi-select chip list. Selecting a category may surface additional required questions (tobacco use, income, hours). When all required questions are answered, a 'See my coverage options' button appears. Clicking it validates the form and, if valid, reveals the product catalog. Changing a category selection or question answer after products are shown collapses the catalog and requires another click.

Each product card lists eligible applicants (member, spouse, child) as checkboxes. Checking an applicant reveals a benefit amount dropdown. DI/OO products also show waiting period and max benefit period dropdowns. Optional riders appear as checkboxes; selecting a rider with an amount range reveals a rider amount dropdown. Coverage selections and amounts are stored per product/applicant key.

If only spouse and/or child are selected for all chosen products (no member selection), clicking Next triggers the onBeforeNext hook and opens a ConfirmationDialog. The user must click Continue to proceed or Cancel to stay on Coverage.
The site can present either 'additional coverage' or 'total coverage' guidance based on the active client configuration.
Coverage categories may start expanded for clients configured with allCategoriesExpanded.

When the user selects their very first product from a state of no selections, the Coverage added AppDrawer opens to show the full cart. For all subsequent product or applicant additions, a compact 'Added' success AppSnackbar appears instead of re-opening the drawer.
The application header shows the coverage cart on application pages except Home and Receipt, and hides it after Review has been submitted.
The cart icon displays a badge count derived from current coverage selections.

definition.rule: Inline cart hidden until a product is selected
definition.behavior: The 'Your requested coverage' inline panel below the Coverage page product catalog shows nothing at all — no section title and no empty-state placeholder — until at least one applicant has an amount selected for a product (grandTotal > 0). The full-drawer cart variant (opened from the header cart icon or the Coverage page's own summary drawer) is unaffected and still shows its 'No coverage selected yet.' empty state.

definition.rule: Quote reveal mirrors Coverage page's category reveal
definition.behavior: Clicking 'See my quote' validates the category-level fields, reveals the matching product cards, and scrolls the drawer so the revealed products land at the top. The 'See my quote' button then hides and reappears only if the user edits a coverage question (gender, tobacco use, income, hours, business expenses/responsibility) or toggles a coverage category selection — the same show/hide contract as the Coverage page's 'See my coverage options' button.

definition.rule: Estimated cost panel uses the shared TotalCostSummary component
definition.behavior: The quote drawer's estimated cost panel now renders via the same TotalCostSummary component used on the Coverage page and in the coverage cart drawer, instead of a bespoke box. Like the Coverage page's inline cart, the panel is hidden entirely until at least one product/applicant has been added (no 'Added coverage will appear here' placeholder); the rate-frequency toggle and Apply button remain visible whenever products are shown.

Apply requires at least one selected product and revalidates the currently applicable quote answers, eligibility facts, benefit amounts and coverage options. Invalid input stays in the quote with an error; membership is collected later. On success, the canonical quote.apply transition initializes the application with collected eligibility and coverage answers, including tobacco follow-ups, contextual employment facts, selected products/applicants, amounts and selected member riders with their amounts. Coverage shows the carried answers as editable values. Home is the only quote entry point; Membership has no quote helper.
When Contact is entered, existing Eligibility location values preset empty Contact location fields without overwriting user-entered Contact values. Targets: state, zip-code.
AppSnackbar appears at top-center on large screens and bottom-center on small screens. Used for Progress Saved and Coverage Added feedback.
Beneficiary records are created only for selected member/spouse LI/AD products with a positive coverage amount and selected applicant.
When Beneficiary mode is optional, the page first asks whether the user wants to add beneficiary information. No skips the beneficiary questions and permits continuation.
When beneficiary questions are active, each applicable product must have at least one beneficiary before continuing.

Clicking 'Add Beneficiary' on a product card opens an AppModal. The modal shows: designation tabs (Primary / Contingent) with a remaining-slot counter; beneficiary type selector (Individual or Trust); and type-specific fields. Individual fields: First Name, Last Name, Relationship, % Share with 25/50/75/100% quick-fill buttons and a live 'X% unassigned remaining' display. Trust fields: Name of Trust and Date of Trust. Clicking Edit pre-populates the modal with the existing record. The 'Add Beneficiary' button is replaced by an info alert when both designations are fully maxed.
Each beneficiary is designated as Primary or Contingent, selected via tabs in the add/edit modal.
A beneficiary can be an Individual or Trust. Within the same Primary/Contingent designation, trust and individual beneficiary types cannot be mixed.
Up to 10 Primary and 10 Contingent beneficiaries may be added per product; reaching 10 prevents additional entries for that designation.
Individual beneficiary share must be greater than 0 and cannot exceed the unassigned percentage remaining for that designation.
Once the assigned individual share reaches 100% for a designation, no more individual beneficiaries can be added for that designation.
Only one Trust may be added per Primary/Contingent designation; if a Trust exists, additional individuals or trusts are blocked for that designation.

After saving a new (not edited) beneficiary, if the same applicant has other eligible products, a second AppModal opens listing those products as checkboxes. The user can select one or more and click 'Apply to Selected', or click Skip. When applied, each target product receives a separate beneficiary record with a new unique ID — not a shared reference.

The captured Contact configuration scopes business fields to selected products when a product list is assigned. Standard WAEPA shows the Business/Employer section with STD and hides it for Life-only; GI retains its separate hiding policy. For visible business addresses, marking the address the same as home reuses the home address. Other DI/OO and correspondence rules retain their configured behavior.

Answers to controlling fields reveal follow-up fields inline within a left-bordered ConditionalGroup container. Changing the controlling answer back collapses the group. Examples: driver license Yes reveals license number/state; is-self-employed Yes reveals self-employment sub-questions; existing life insurance Yes reveals amount and replacement fields. Some follow-ups are themselves controls for deeper nested groups.

When the user indicates existing disability coverage, insurance company records are added through the DynamicList pattern: existing records show as bordered cards; Add opens an AppModal with company name, monthly benefit amount, benefit period, and waiting period fields; Edit pre-populates the modal; Remove requires a confirmation modal.
Member and spouse outside-U.S. residence/travel questions reveal country/month follow-ups only for affirmative responses.

Financial questionnaire visibility follows the active site’s MCR product-question-set assignments (Main column Y), for a selected member product with a positive amount. Sites without an assigned financial questionnaire omit this section. The former DI amount greater than $2,000 trigger was prototype demo behavior, not a general rule. Self-employment details appear when is-self-employed = Yes.
Member/spouse health sections follow applicant-applying visibility; the member section label is hidden for member-only flow.

Each health question is a required Yes/No radio. Selecting Yes reveals a DynamicList inline below that question where the user can add one or more detail records (onset date, condition/medication details, physician/hospital address) via the standard Add/Edit/Remove modal pattern. Selecting No collapses and clears the list for that question.
When Payment mode is optional, the page first asks whether the user wants to add payment information; No permits continuation without payment questions.
When payment questions are active, each applicable product requires a payment method and payment frequency before continuing.
Bank-account details (name on account, institution, routing number, account number, authorization checkbox) are displayed when Bank account is selected as the payment method for any product.

Clicking an edit icon opens a ConfirmationDialog. Confirming navigates back to the page that owns that information. In advisor-applicant flow the same action instead opens a SendApplicationDialog ('Request edit to application') showing the advisor email; sending navigates to Application Edit Confirmation.

AppDrawer slides in from the right on desktop (420–480px wide) or up from the bottom on mobile (75vh). Used for contextual help topics (HelpChips → AppDrawer), the QuickDecision℠ explainer, the Coverage Portfolio (TPA-verified users on Coverage), and the application menu sub-drawers (coverage options, needs calculator, QD explainer). Drawers are read-only and do not block page submission.
The swipeable prop enables SwipeableDrawer on mobile for user-initiated drawers (e.g. the Coverage cart drawer). Non-swipeable drawers use a standard Drawer.

DynamicList is the shared component for any repeatable record set (children, insurance companies, health detail records). Existing records render as bordered DynamicListItem cards with Edit and Remove buttons. Add opens an AppModal titled 'Add [Label]' with a blank form. Edit opens the same modal pre-filled with the selected record. Save appends or updates the record. Remove shows a confirmation AppModal ('Remove [Label]?') and deletes on confirm. Fields inside the modal are defined per record type via a mapping prop and rendered by FieldRenderer. The Add button is hidden once maxItems is reached (default 10).

New Application mode displays advisor credential fields on Advisor Login. When the advisor later clicks Next on Profile, the onBeforeNext hook opens a SendApplicationDialog titled 'Send to applicant for review' showing the applicant name and email. Clicking Send navigates to Advisor Send Confirmation; Cancel stays on Profile.

Saved Application mode displays applicant email on Advisor Login. In advisor-applicant flow, clicking an edit icon on Review opens a SendApplicationDialog titled 'Request edit to application' showing the advisor email only. Clicking Send navigates to Application Edit Confirmation; Cancel stays on Review.

default = inline Quote Tool and no hero image; hero-image = hero image, no inline Quote Tool; welcome-back = hero image, Continue/New Application actions, and hides How Applying Works and Coverage Options.
Default and hero-image variants display the saved-application resume prompt/link; welcome-back uses Continue Application as the primary action instead.

The app header hides when the user scrolls down (threshold: 8px) and reappears immediately on any upward scroll. Implemented via MUI useScrollTrigger + Slide direction='down'. The header uses position='sticky' so it participates in document layout rather than overlapping content.
Application header supports Chat (when enabled and eligible), Coverage Cart and Menu. It does not contain a Quote action in the latest source.
The Chat and Coverage Cart header actions are hidden once ApplicationSessionContext reports that review was submitted, in addition to being hidden on the Home and Receipt pages.

CookieDialog is shown as a fixed bottom banner on first visit. AppShell checks localStorage.cookieConsent !== 'accepted' to decide whether to render it; dismissing sets localStorage.cookieConsent = 'accepted' so it never reappears.
AppBody patches window.history.pushState/replaceState and listens for popstate to track the current pathname, then scrolls the window to top on every route change.

When ApplicationSessionContext is in advisor-applicant mode (the applicant entered via resume?flow=advisor), the stepper/breadcrumb progress UI locks navigation to all steps except application-review and esign-submit, regardless of completed state.

FieldRenderer live-formats input as the user types based on field.format: currency ('$1,234'), percent, phone (parenthesized area code), ssn (dashes, with all but the most-recently-typed digit masked for ~800ms), and month-year. The date input type is also formatted inline.

definition.rule: Auto label variant for long labels
definition.behavior: FieldRenderer auto-selects a 'standard' (external) label instead of the default 'floating' label when field.label is 40+ characters, to avoid clipping, unless field.labelVariant is explicitly set.
Phone-format fields render an inline Mobile/Home/Business type selector tied to a sibling field (field.phoneTypeFieldId, default '<field.id>-type'), unless field.showPhoneTypeSelector is false.

definition.rule: Auto search-select for long option lists
definition.behavior: FieldRenderer renders a field configured as inputType: 'dropdown' using the searchable-select (MUI Autocomplete) component instead of a plain Select once field.options has 10 or more entries, so long lists (e.g. US states) are searchable rather than requiring a long scroll. Fields already explicitly set to 'searchable-select' are unaffected.

definition.rule: Panel page/drawer variant with nested sub-drawers
definition.behavior: HowApplyingWorksPanel and CoverageOptionsPanel accept a variant: 'page' | 'drawer' prop rendering the same content as a full page section or a compact drawer layout. In 'drawer' variant, HowApplyingWorksPanel manages its own nested sub-drawer state (Application Review / QuickDecision℠) stacked above the parent drawer; in 'page' variant those links call parent-supplied handlers instead.

definition.rule: Coverage Options featured-first sort and category fallback
definition.behavior: Default category order is LI, AD, DI, OO, SH. A client coverages.categoryOrder (or categories array) configuration overrides it. A client coverages.productOrder optionally overrides product order within categories; omitted products retain the default order. AMA uses its source 20/15/10-year, Pure Term, Preferred Term, Premier Accident order; URL parameter featured_prod moves the identified product’s category first and that product first within it. Default products are Term Life, ascending level-term durations; Long-Term, Long-Term Plus, Mid-Term, Short-Term Disability; Critical Illness, Hospital Indemnity. Remaining products retain catalog order. An unavailable active category falls back to the first available category in the resolved order.

Menu provides Continue Saved Application, How Applying Works, About Coverage, Needs Calculator, About QuickDecision and client Contact information. Each tool closes the main menu drawer and opens a standalone AppDrawer (How Applying Works and About Coverage render HowApplyingWorksPanel / CoverageOptionsPanel in 'drawer' variant).
When Spouse is selected as a dependent, display the applicant-specific spouse sections and fields; post-Coverage applicant selection gates still apply separately.

definition.behavior: The applicant recovery service owns save retention, link and code expiry, incorrect-attempt and issue/request limits, revocation, single-use verification and write-capability rotation. definition.rule: Revalidate saved applications after Library revision changes
definition.behavior: A recovered or locally remembered save whose Library revision differs requires explicit Coverage or Review completion before mock submission. Ordinary autosaves do not clear that state. The save service and applicant submission check own this client-assisted mock behavior; no warning banner is required.

definition.rule: Product eligibility and benefit limits use captured policies
definition.behavior: Product eligibility constraints, scoped Association eligibility, additional eligibility facts, structured amount assignments, benefit policies and selection/dependent policies own their respective decisions. Explicit Site/product/Association/applicant assignments determine applicability. Association residency lists and identifier roles use their dedicated captured policies. This record references those owners; individual requirements still need semantic coverage verification.

definition.rule: Billing and premium modifiers use captured product policies
definition.behavior: Captured product rate modifier policies and journey billing policies own membership adjustments, billing factors and applicable fees. The rating and billing resolvers execute them; rule prose does not supply competing values.

definition.rule: Fraud notice follows the captured Review policy
definition.behavior: The Site Review policy owns jurisdiction text and scoped product exceptions. resolveFraudNotice selects the applicable notice using residence and selected products; missing residence is not silently assigned a jurisdiction.

rules.sourceReference: Rules owner crosswalk October 20, 2026; existing implemented behavior

definition.rule: Consent blocks follow captured applicability and fields
definition.behavior: The captured Review policy owns applicant, product and application-mode conditions for consent blocks, source consent selection and role-specific openings. Active block field definitions own required acknowledgements; the Review resolver and page execute applicability and validation.

After 43 minutes of inactivity, display a warning above the application with a live countdown. Form activity extends the deadline. The 45-minute inactivity limit and 2-minute warning are provisional prototype timing; neither checked-in MCR extract specifies a limit. Confirm with the session service before production.

At the inactivity deadline, or when the application service reports an expired session, reload to the Session expired utility page. Stop the form flow and offer Resume application and Start new application. Resume uses the secure recovery flow and starts a new session after successful verification. Starting a new application clears local application values and session state. Saved progress is retained by the application service; unsaved changes are not guaranteed.

For network or server failures while saving, calculating rates, submitting or authorizing payment, display a page error alert directing the applicant to resume from their last saved progress. Validation and eligibility failures retain their specific feedback. Unhandled rendering errors use the 500 utility page; unknown routes use 404. Both include the shared application recovery actions.

Provide a shared maintenance page with the current Site identity and Questions support card. Explain temporary unavailability without inventing a return time or claiming that unsaved changes were saved. Show a logo-only recovery header and no navigation actions while the Site is unavailable. The prototype route is /maintenance; automatic activation requires an authoritative availability signal from the host or application service.

Every maintenance and error page includes the shared Questions support card with the resolved Site administrator, phone, email and website when configured. Email and site cards share contact resolution and common labels. Email-only hideContactBox settings do not suppress required support on recovery pages. Page and inline technical errors use the same recovery message source, and start-new remains the only recovery action that clears local application state.

definition.title: Consumer Application Flow
definition.intro: Shows the stable consumer application backbone. Page inclusion and page contents are resolved by client configuration, applicant data, selected coverage, underwriting requirements, and enabled riders. Conditional coverage behavior, field/section variations, and health-page routing are documented in their configuration/routing sections rather than selectively expanded in this backbone flow.

definition.title: Advisor-Assisted Flow
definition.intro: The advisor completes the application through Profile and transfers it to the applicant for review and final completion. Only one actor may access the application at a time.

definition.title: Resume & Verification Flow
definition.intro: Restores an incomplete application through an email-based secure link and phone verification code.

definition.title: Autosave & Persistence Flow
definition.intro: Autosave begins after successful Membership submission. Field-level saving by external underwriting experiences is outside Portal autosave scope.

definition.title: Quote Flow
definition.intro: Available through configured entry points (drawer/modal, not a standalone page). Collects minimum information to determine available products and estimated premiums.

definition.title: TPA Member Verification Flow
definition.intro: After membership attestation, use the configured prototype TPA lookup. Existing members with active coverage proceed to simulated identity verification. AMA uses First Name, Last Name and DOB. ASCE also requires Membership ID and state; when matched, an alert collects the full residential address before the member verification modal opens. A pass enables the coverage portfolio; failure or skipping continues without a portfolio. No real verification provider is required for the prototype.

definition.title: TPA Member Verification Flow
definition.intro: ASCE lookup uses Membership ID, First Name, Last Name, DOB and state. When triggered, collect the full residential address before opening member verification. Existing member + active coverage proceeds to LexisNexis; pass enables portfolio and TPA auto-approval, fail/skipped goes to TPA admin manual review without a portfolio.

definition.label: Landing Page
definition.description: Starts a new application, opens Quote, or resumes an application.

definition.label: Membership
definition.description: Collects membership and applicant contact information. Establishes application record and starts autosave.

definition.label: Eligibility
definition.description: Collects ZIP/postal code, state, date of birth, dependent selection, and configured eligibility responses.

definition.label: Coverage
definition.description: Collects eligible applicants, products, amounts, riders, and estimated premiums. Available choices and downstream requirements vary by selected coverage and client configuration.

definition.label: Beneficiary
definition.description: Included when selected coverage is configured for beneficiary designation (Required/Optional/None mode).

definition.label: Contact
definition.description: Collects configured applicant, mailing, business, and spouse contact information.

definition.label: Profile
definition.description: Collects configured personal, employment, financial, existing-coverage, travel, residence, and spouse information.

definition.label: Review
definition.description: Presents application summary and required consent/acknowledgement sections.

definition.label: Health Routing
definition.description: Applicable health forms are resolved independently from selected coverage and underwriting type. See Health Routing below for the condition-to-page mapping.

definition.label: Payment
definition.description: Collects payment information when included by Required or Optional page mode.

definition.label: E-Sign
definition.description: Completes the configured electronic-signature process (DocuSign).

definition.label: Receipt
definition.description: Displays submission confirmation, decision information, and configured next steps.

definition.label: Resume saved application (Advisor)
definition.description: Enter applicant email, open the secure link and complete resume verification.

definition.label: Resume delivery method (Advisor)
definition.description: After opening the secure email link, choose Text or Call for the verification code.

definition.label: Resume Code (Advisor)
definition.description: Load the saved application and return to Eligibility.

definition.label: Advisor Login
definition.description: Start opens Membership. Continue opens Resume for a saved application.

definition.label: Membership
definition.description: Advisor begins application.

definition.label: Eligibility
definition.description: Advisor completes eligibility information.

definition.label: Coverage
definition.description: Advisor completes coverage selections.

definition.label: Beneficiary (if applicable)
definition.description: Advisor completes beneficiary information when included in resolved flow.

definition.label: Contact
definition.description: Advisor completes contact information.

definition.label: Profile
definition.description: Advisor completes the final advisor page.

definition.label: Send Application Dialog
definition.description: After clicking Next on Profile, advisor sees SendApplicationDialog titled 'Send to applicant for review' with applicant name + email and send-confirmation copy.

definition.label: Advisor Send Confirmation
definition.description: Confirmation page showing the applicant email, send timestamp, and purge date. Advisor can start a new application.

definition.label: Resume & Verification (Applicant)
definition.description: Applicant enters via resume?flow=advisor, submits email and proceeds to Review without the verification-code step in the current prototype.

definition.label: Review (advisor mode)
definition.description: Applicant reviews advisor-entered application data on the standard Review page (flow=advisor). Earlier stepper steps are locked.

definition.label: Applicant requests edit?
definition.description: Edit icon on Review (advisor mode) opens the edit-request dialog.

definition.label: Request Edit Dialog
definition.description: SendApplicationDialog titled 'Request edit to application' with advisor email only and alert copy.

definition.label: Application Edit Confirmation
definition.description: Confirms the edit request was sent to the advisor dummy email. Application lock transfers back to the advisor; applicant access ends here.

definition.label: Health Routing
definition.description: Applicable health forms as separate routes grouped under one Health progress stage — see Health Routing below for per-condition detail.

definition.label: Payment
definition.description: Collects payment information when included by Required or Optional page mode.

definition.label: E-Sign
definition.description: Completes the configured electronic-signature process (DocuSign).

definition.label: Receipt
definition.description: Displays submission confirmation, decision information, and configured next steps.

definition.label: Resume Request
definition.description: User enters application email address; reminder-email links prefill it.

definition.label: Request Confirmation
definition.description: System shows same confirmation whether or not a matching application is found.

definition.label: Resume Link
definition.description: User opens the time-limited email link.

definition.label: Resume Method
definition.description: User selects how to receive their verification code: Text or Call.

definition.label: Resume Code
definition.description: User enters the security code sent via the chosen delivery method.

definition.label: Verification Result
definition.description: Displays success or failure.

definition.label: Restored Destination
definition.description: User is routed to the next incomplete page.

definition.label: Membership Submission
definition.description: Autosave begins after successful Membership submission for both consumer and advisor applications.

definition.label: Page Submission
definition.description: Portal form data is saved when a page is successfully submitted.

definition.label: Save outcome?
definition.description: Whether the autosave request for the submitted page completed successfully.

definition.label: Save Confirmed
definition.description: Saved indicator appears only after the save is confirmed.

definition.label: Save Failure — Recovery Scenarios (10)
definition.description: Network connectivity failure; server/application error; API or service unavailability; session expiration; validation failure; database persistence failure; concurrent update conflict; browser interruption; storage limit exceeded; partial save failure. The source documentation gives no distinct downstream destination per scenario, so these are summarized here rather than modeled as separate branches.

definition.label: Entry Point
definition.description: Available from Landing Page and Membership page (drawer/modal, not standalone page).

definition.label: Collect Inputs
definition.description: Collects minimum information required: DOB, gender, tobacco status, category-specific inputs.

definition.label: Calculate Estimates
definition.description: Calculates estimated premiums for supported categories (LI, AD, DI, OO, SH).

definition.label: Product Selection
definition.description: At least one product must be selected before continuing into application — a validation gate, not a routing branch.

definition.label: Carry into Application
definition.description: Applicable quote inputs and selected products carry into the application fields.

definition.label: Membership attestation
definition.description: Applicant claims membership eligibility before the TPA lookup.

definition.label: TPA Eligibility Lookup
definition.description: Look up First Name, Last Name and DOB, plus any configured additional fields. Return existing-member and active-coverage status.

definition.label: Existing member + active coverage?
definition.description: Both conditions must be true to offer LexisNexis identity verification.

definition.label: Regular Application — No Portfolio
definition.description: No existing member or no active coverage. Continue without a coverage portfolio; submission goes to the TPA admin for manual review.

definition.label: Choose Verification Method
definition.description: Applicant may verify by text code, voice code, or security questions, or proceed without verification.

definition.label: LexisNexis Security Questions
definition.description: Three identity questions are presented. Selecting a none-of-the-above response causes verification failure.

definition.label: Verification successful?
definition.description: A completed verification attempt resolves to success or failure.

I (or the certificate owner, if different) understand and agree that any dividend apportioned to the group policy may be retained by the American Bar Endowment to support its charitable work in the field of law unless such dividends are claimed by me (or the certificate owner) pursuant to the procedures described in the the plan brochures, on the back of the ABE premium notices, in each November issue of the ABA Journal, and in the plan description material on the ABE website (http://abendowment.org/forms/assignment.asp). (Notice of the approximate percentage premium available, if any, for contribution or refund will be published in the November issue of the ABA Journal.) The Internal Revenue Service has ruled that members who donate their dividends to ABE are eligible for a charitable contribution deduction on their individual income tax returns.

Founded by the ABA in 1942, the American Bar Endowment is a §501(c) (3) not-for-profit organization composed of members of the American Bar Association. ABE fulfills its charitable purpose of improving the administration of justice, one of our profession’s highest obligations, by making annual grants to support legal research, public service and educational projects in the field of law, including those conducted by ABA’s Fund for Justice and Education (FJE) and the American Bar Foundation (ABF). ABE also maintains a Legal Legacy Fund for the permanent support of its grantees. By participating in the Endowment's group insurance programs, designed for and available only to ABA members, members can contribute to these efforts.Members who enroll in ABE-sponsored insurance programs agree that their share of any dividends payable on the group policies may be retained by ABE for its charitable purposes unless reclaimed as outlined below. The Internal Revenue Service has ruled that members who donate their dividends to ABE are eligible for a charitable contribution deduction on+A16 their individual income tax returns. Contributions to ABE are tax deductible under Section 170(c) of the U.S. Internal Revenue Code, in accordance with IRS regulations and the March 1987 ruling provided to ABE by the IRS.

Members who donate dividends to ABE make a difference. These funds, after administrative expenses, are the primary source of ABE's charitable grants and additions to the Legal Legacy Fund. Insured members who donate their dividends help meet their professional and public responsibilities, as well as obtaining valuable coverage for their families. About 85% of members donate their dividends; these members are notified each year by late January of the amount, if any, of their dividend donation for the prior year. (Dividends are not guaranteed, and in any given year, a given plan may not pay a dividend; dividends will vary from year to year.)

Members who wish to request a refund of their dividends may do so. The approximate percentage of premium available for refund (if any) on each plan will be published in each November issue of the ABA Journal. You do not need to wait for this information as refund requests are accepted beginning January 1. To request that dividends be paid to you rather than donated to ABE: After the first policy year of your participation, a written request for refund (by mail, fax, or email to dividends@abendowment.org) must be made each year and must reach the Endowment by December 15. When ABE receives your refund request, it will send a confirmation. Retain this for your records as proof your request was timely received. If you do not receive a confirmation within 3 weeks, contact the ABE promptly to obtain another copy. (Special instructions for new applicants are contained in the application and apply to dividends, if any, during the first policy year only.)

Dividend checks and/or contribution notices for your tax return are mailed by late January. If you receive a contribution notice and you did not intend to make a contribution, you may request a one-time waiver of the December 15 deadline by asking for a refund, if you have not previously requested such a waiver.

Please note: Members who do not want to contribute dividends to ABE must make a written request for refund each year, using the procedures above. When members sign the application, they are agreeing to make an annual decision whether to contribute. Do not sign the application if you do not agree with these procedures.

The Consent covers your agreement to all of the terms and conditions of the Consent, including your agreement to:
1.    execute via electronic means any documents that New York Life requires to be signed in connection with the application process for this Insurance Certificate (the “Application Forms”);

2.    be bound with the same force and effect as if you had affixed your signature on paper, by hand, when you click “Submit” and apply your electronic signature or otherwise apply your electronic signature to the Application Forms;
